$comment: Third-party MCP servers evaluated BY USE for SignalGrid (docs/agent/RESOURCE_INTAKE.md rules). Every entry was cloned at the pinned sha, read for what it reads/writes/sends/hooks, built, and probed over stdio with every socket denied. None runs from this repository's .mcp.json (it carries only signalgrid-mcp) and none may enter the decision path. The four live-lane servers are aids for the Mac lane's rehearsal, added to a PERSON'S user-level MCP config by hand, never to a hook; context7 is the one exception in kind — a dev-docs aid both lanes register at user scope through `pnpm run mcp:setup` (scripts/install-context7.mjs), still never .mcp.json and never a hook. Measured 2026-09-18 on the cloud lane; context7 row measured 2026-09-19 on the Mac.
landing: Documented, registered by hand at USER scope on the machine that needs it (`claude mcp add … --scope user`), the same way the parity doc treats GitHub; never .mcp.json, never a hook, never the decision path. No installer script: an automated registration into a session config was refused by the harness on 2026-09-18, and the manual command is one line.

servers.matches: dependency work on both lanes — current library docs before a version or API change (signalgrid-master, Supply chain and dependencies)
servers.reads: nothing on disk; the library name, pinned version and question the agent sends
servers.network: context7.com over HTTPS, keyless (CONTEXT7_API_KEY optional, never set here); a failed or 429 fetch is returned as an error string, the tool never throws (packages/mcp/src/lib/api.ts)
servers.build: npm i @upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1, prebuilt dist; boots in under 1 s
servers.offline: boots and lists both tools (resolve-library-id, query-docs; readOnlyHint true on each) with sockets denied via sandbox-exec; identical to the online run
servers.reason: keyless, read-only, pinned; the only doc-lookup both lanes share. Unreachable means 'docs not checked', never a loosened claim — the skill line says so.
servers.config: pnpm run mcp:setup  (runs scripts/install-context7.mjs: claude mcp add context7 --scope user -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1)

servers.reads: the Wazuh manager API and indexer named by WAZUH_API_HOST/PORT and WAZUH_INDEXER_HOST/PORT with the credentials in WAZUH_API_USERNAME/PASSWORD and WAZUH_INDEXER_USERNAME/PASSWORD; WAZUH_VERIFY_SSL
servers.network: only the two Wazuh endpoints it is configured with
servers.offline: boots and lists all 14 tools with sockets denied; identical on two runs
servers.reason: read-only by construction (every tool is a get_/search_ read; no POST/PUT/DELETE in src), env-configured, deterministic tool surface. Lets the Mac lane read the live Wazuh it already runs during a live-edr rehearsal.
servers.config: claude mcp add wazuh --scope user --env WAZUH_API_HOST=… --env WAZUH_API_PORT=55000 --env WAZUH_INDEXER_HOST=… --env WAZUH_INDEXER_PORT=9200 --env WAZUH_API_USERNAME=<read-only user> --env WAZUH_API_PASSWORD=<from the keychain> --env WAZUH_INDEXER_USERNAME=… --env WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD=… -- <path to target/release/mcp-server-wazuh built at the pinned sha under ~/.cache/signalgrid/>

servers.reads: the Keycloak Admin REST API at KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL/KEYCLOAK_REALM, authenticating with AUTH_MODE=password (KC_ADMIN_USERNAME/PASSWORD/REALM) or service_account (KC_CLIENT_ID/SECRET)
servers.writes: nothing on disk; 31 of 56 tools WRITE to Keycloak (create, delete, assign, unassign, update, set-enabled, reset-password, logout, sync)
servers.offline: boots and lists all 56 tools with sockets denied once AUTH_MODE and the KC_ADMIN_* variables are set; refuses to start without them; identical on two runs
servers.reason: an ADMIN server: more than half its tools mutate the realm. The read-only doctrine has no way to switch those off, and a Keycloak the live lane stands up and tears down does not need administering by an agent. If a read-only fork or an allow-list flag appears upstream, re-evaluate.

servers.matches: the operator surfaces (admin console, operator console, PWA, public site) — the screen inventory and demo-path brief row in BUILD_BACKLOG
servers.reads: whatever page it is pointed at, through the pre-installed Chromium
servers.writes: nothing on disk by default (screenshots/traces only where the caller asks)
servers.network: the pages it is pointed at; no telemetry endpoint in src
servers.build: npm ci --ignore-scripts, 3 s; runs against /opt/pw-browsers/chromium with --executable-path
servers.offline: boots and lists all 26 tools with sockets denied; identical on two runs
servers.reason: official, no env, no writes, pinned package. The one server that serves the design gap directly: it can walk every screen of the consoles and hand back accessibility snapshots and screenshots for the inventory. Local pages only — it must never be pointed at a tenant's live console.
servers.config: claude mcp add playwright --scope user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@0.0.81 --headless --browser chromium  (add --executable-path /opt/pw-browsers/chromium on the cloud lane; on a Mac run `npx playwright install chromium` once first)

servers.matches: the durable audit ledger (Postgres) in the deploy stack
servers.reads: DATABASE_URL (or MCP_DATABASE_URLS); 44 MCP_* knobs for allow-lists, redaction, rate limits, audit HMAC
servers.writes: an audit log on disk when MCP_AUDIT_LOG is set (src/audit_log.rs)
servers.network: only the database URL; sets default_transaction_read_only and a statement timeout
servers.offline: REFUSES to serve without a reachable database: logs 'DB CONNECT FAILED' plus a signed posture line and never answers tools/list (fail-closed, the right shape). Tool count therefore unmeasured here.
servers.reason: read-only by construction and fail-closed, but it needs the live Postgres the deploy-stack CI job or the Mac lane stands up; re-measure the tool surface there before adopting.
